review_notes: I read the whole file. It has two theorems and no simp attributes. I also read the nearby definitions and uses. `mem_vec3Ball` is already `@[simp]` and is `Iff.rfl`, in Foundation/Parabolic/Basic.lean. `closure_vec3Ball` is a plain theorem with `0 < r` as a hypothesis, in Foundation/Parabolic/Topology.lean. `euclideanBall_eq_vec3Ball_of_pos` is used with explicit `rw [... (by positivity : 0 < ρ/2)]` in PressureGradientOriginClauseGauge, WeakGradientGluingTBounds and others. I did not recommend making it a simp lemma. Its positivity side condition is usually a compound expression such as `13 * ρ / 20`, which simp's default discharger may not prove. A new simp rule from `euclideanBall` to `vec3Ball` would also change normal forms for other users of `euclideanBall`. I saw no credible loop, competing simp rule, wrong rewrite direction or unwanted expansion in this file. The proof of the first theorem unfolds definitions with `simp only`, but that stays inside the proof and does not affect any simp interface. A near-duplicate of `euclideanBall_eq_vec3Ball_of_pos` exists as `CKN.Foundation.Parabolic.euclideanBall_eq_vec3Ball` in BallBasics.lean, along with private copies in other files. That is a duplication or organisation issue, not a simp-interface defect, so I did not report it under this rubric. I could not run Lean, so I cannot rule out other simp-normal-form effects.
